beats.narration: Begin by framing Introduction to Machine Learning Workflow as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Consider this worked case: A developer uses a pipeline to standardize features, train a classifier, and evaluate accuracy without mixing training and testing data. On screen, display a horizontal flowchart with six labeled nodes connected by arrows, representing the sequential workflow stages. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
beats.title: Introduction to Machine Learning Workflow
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a horizontal flowchart with six labeled nodes connected by arrows, representing the sequential workflow stages.

beats.narration: Now define Data Preparation and Leakage Prevention precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Consider this worked case: Scaling features using the mean and standard deviation calculated solely from the training set before splitting the data. On screen, show a split diagram with 'Training Data' and 'Test Data' boxes, highlighting that preprocessing parameters are derived exclusively from the training box. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
beats.title: Data Preparation and Leakage Prevention
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a split diagram with 'Training Data' and 'Test Data' boxes, highlighting that preprocessing parameters are derived exclusively from the training box.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Supervised vs. Unsupervised Learning operates in a concrete sequence. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Consider this worked case: Classifying email as spam or ham uses labeled data, whereas clustering customers by purchasing behavior uses unlabeled data. On screen, present two side-by-side icons: a labeled dataset with a target column for supervised learning, and a scatter plot of unlabeled points for unsupervised learning. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
beats.title: Supervised vs. Unsupervised Learning
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present two side-by-side icons: a labeled dataset with a target column for supervised learning, and a scatter plot of unlabeled points for unsupervised learning.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Statistical Analysis and Data Visualization and make the decision criteria explicit. Topics include: Mathematical background of machine learning (for example statistical analysis and visualization of data), Bayesian decision theory, parametric and non-parameteric classification models (for example, SVMs and Nearest Neighbor models) and neural network models (for example Convolutional, Recurrent, and Deep Neural Networks). Consider this worked case: Plotting a histogram and box plot to detect outliers and skewness before selecting a regression model. On screen, render a composite image showing a histogram, a box plot, and a scatter plot with a regression line, each labeled with its statistical purpose. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: Statistical Analysis and Data Visualization
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Render a composite image showing a histogram, a box plot, and a scatter plot with a regression line, each labeled with its statistical purpose.

beats.narration: Apply Bayesian Decision Theory to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Consider this worked case: Calculating the posterior probability of a medical diagnosis given a test result, using prior prevalence and test sensitivity/specificity. On screen, illustrate a Bayesian update cycle with three boxes: Prior, Likelihood, and Posterior, connected by arrows showing probability adjustment. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Bayesian Decision Theory
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a Bayesian update cycle with three boxes: Prior, Likelihood, and Posterior, connected by arrows showing probability adjustment.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Parametric Classification Models, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. An introduction to both foundational and modern machine learning theories and algorithms, and their application in classification and regression. Consider this worked case: Training an SVM on a dataset of handwritten digits to draw a hyperplane that separates correct from incorrect digit classifications. On screen, draw a 2D scatter plot with a straight decision boundary line, highlighting the margin distance between the boundary and the nearest data points. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
beats.title: Parametric Classification Models
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Draw a 2D scatter plot with a straight decision boundary line, highlighting the margin distance between the boundary and the nearest data points.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Non-Parametric Classification Models with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Unsupervised methods identify structure without target labels. Consider this worked case: Assigning a new customer to a segment by finding the three closest historical customers in feature space and taking their majority class. On screen, show a 2D plot with a query point surrounded by a circle, highlighting the three nearest training points and their assigned labels. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Non-Parametric Classification Models
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a 2D plot with a query point surrounded by a circle, highlighting the three nearest training points and their assigned labels.

beats.narration: Use Neural Network Architectures to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Risk analysis considers data quality and uncertainty. Consider this worked case: Using a Convolutional Neural Network to detect edges and textures in images, or a Recurrent Neural Network to predict the next word in a sentence sequence. On screen, display a simplified diagram of a three-layer neural network with input, hidden, and output nodes, showing weighted connections and activation functions. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
beats.title: Neural Network Architectures
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a simplified diagram of a three-layer neural network with input, hidden, and output nodes, showing weighted connections and activation functions.

beats.narration: Connect Model Evaluation and Hyperparameter Selection to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Consider this worked case: Using precision and recall for imbalanced classification tasks, and tuning learning rate via cross-validation before testing on held-out data. On screen, show a confusion matrix and a learning curve graph, with annotations indicating metric selection and cross-validation folds. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Model Evaluation and Hyperparameter Selection
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a confusion matrix and a learning curve graph, with annotations indicating metric selection and cross-validation folds.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness. Consider this worked case: Before deployment, verify that preprocessing parameters were not fitted on test data, check for bias in predictions across demographic groups, and schedule post-deployment monitoring. On screen, list a five-item checklist with checkboxes: Data Quality Verified, Leakage Prevented, Metrics Matched, Fairness Audited, Monitoring Scheduled. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | List a five-item checklist with checkboxes: Data Quality Verified, Leakage Prevented, Metrics Matched, Fairness Audited, Monitoring Scheduled.

sources.author: scikit-learn developers
sources.excerpt: Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Unsupervised methods identify structure without target labels. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Pipelines combine preprocessing and estimators so the same transformations are applied consistently. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined data splits. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Hyperparameter selection must remain separate from final test evaluation. Leakage, distribution shift, overfitting, and unexamined assumptions can invalidate results.
sources.title: scikit-learn User Guide

sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.excerpt: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Govern establishes policies, responsibilities, and accountability for AI risk. Map documents context, intended use, affected people, and potential impacts. Measure uses qualitative and quantitative methods to analyze identified risks. Manage prioritizes risks and allocates resources for response and monitoring. Risk analysis considers data quality and uncertainty. It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness. Monitoring continues after deployment because context and system behavior can change.
sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
